standard_prerequisites.use: Final step (source lines 2014-2016): an invertible sheaf with a nonzero global section is trivial, by the Varieties criterion.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 2004-2009): for a proper curve X over a field k with H^0(X, O_X) = k and genus 0, every invertible O_X-module L of degree 0 is trivial.
Riemann-Roch application (proof lines 2011-2013): by Lemma lemma-rr, dim_k H^0(X, L) >= h^1(L) + deg(L) - g + 1 >= 0 + 1 - 0 = 1, using deg(L) = 0, g = 0 and h^1(L) >= 0.
Trivialization (lines 2013-2016): hence L has a nonzero global section, and L cong O_X by the Varieties trivialization criterion.
proof_roadmap: Apply the Riemann-Roch inequality with deg 0 and genus 0.
Trivialize the invertible module by the standard criterion.
difficulty_reason: Vanishing/triviality lemma (statement 2004-2009, proof 2011-2016): on a genus zero curve every degree zero invertible module is trivial - the proof is the Riemann-Roch inequality evaluated at deg 0, g = 0 (the in-span computation dim H^0 >= 1) followed by the standard nonzero-section trivialization; short but complete, no step omitted. H2: short computation plus standard criterion.
